questions.q: In the AI Safety via Debate protocol, what is supposed to produce a trustworthy outcome?
options: Both debaters being programmed to always tell the truth
The adversarial structure itself — neither debater is assumed honest by design
The judge always being a more capable model than either debater
A coin flip that decides the winner regardless of argument quality
questions.explain: Debate is designed so that the structure of adversarial argument, not either debater's assumed honesty, is what's meant to surface a trustworthy result.

questions.q: What theoretical asymmetry does debate's core bet rely on?
options: That generating a correct answer is always easier than checking a specific claim
That it's often easier to check a specific claim or spot a specific flaw than to independently produce a fully correct answer unassisted
That judges are always more capable than either debater
That there is no difference in effort between verifying and generating an answer
questions.explain: The verifying-is-easier-than-generating asymmetry is the theoretical foundation debate rests on.

questions.q: What have empirical debate experiments, such as Anthropic's scalable oversight measurements, actually found so far?
options: Debate always perfectly outperforms every baseline on every task tested
Results are mixed and task-dependent, with some advantage over simpler baselines but not a large or consistent one across every domain tested
Debate has never once been tested with real language models
Debate performs worse than random guessing in all tested conditions
questions.explain: Real experiments show a task-dependent, inconsistent advantage over baselines like consultancy, not a uniform win for debate.

options: A technical bug that crashes debate software during long exchanges
The concern that a sufficiently capable debater could make a false position more persuasive than a true one within the judge's actual time and attention, even though a flaw exists
The requirement that debate transcripts be encrypted before judging
A proven mathematical theorem showing debate never works
questions.explain: This is the core open concern with debate: persuasiveness and correctness might not track each other closely enough for the judge to reliably find the truth.

questions.q: According to this lesson, has it been settled whether debate reliably converges to true answers as debaters and tasks get harder?
options: Yes, multiple studies have definitively proven debate always converges to truth
No — this is described as a genuinely open empirical question that current experiments have not settled either way
Yes, it has been definitively proven that debate never converges to truth
This question has never been raised in any research on debate
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that whether debate reliably surfaces truth, versus just rewarding better argumentation, remains an open and contested empirical question.
